Hi Jordan / Elena —

Thanks again for taking the demo today — great conversation and really helpful context on the high-volume customer support use case and latency targets (~120ms p50 for chat flows). Per our discussion, I pulled together a short recommended model shortlist with tradeoffs across cost, latency, and quality. I attached a one-page PDF and the first prompt set we used for the evals. Summary below: 

Recommended shortlist (first-pass):
- Llama-3 8B (4-bit quantized) — Best cost/latency sweet spot. ~2-3x cheaper than 13B variants, p50 latency approx 90-120ms on our dedicated 80GB A10G pool; strong on intent classification and short-answer quality after a light prompt tuning step.
- Redwood-2 13B (FP16) — Higher quality on multi-turn instruction following and complex summarization; p50 ~160-220ms, better at edge-case hallucination avoidance. Good if you prioritize quality over raw token cost.
- Mistral-Instruct 7B (8-bit) — Lightweight alternative with crisp generation on support prompts, extremely low cost, p50 ~80-110ms; may require prompt engineering for longer context stability.

Key notes / risks:
- Quality regression monitoring: we recommend running the supplied prompt set (attached) plus your top 200 production queries as a regression baseline before any rollout. We'll provide automated evals and alerts via Redwood Optimize.
- Prefix/KV caching: for repeated conversational contexts we can save ~25-40% token cost; will need to instrument the client to send conversation ids.
- Quantized models (4-bit) have slightly higher variance on rare tokens; recommended canary on a small % of traffic for 48-72 hours.

Attachments: ACME_model_shortlist_20260615.pdf (one-pager), ACME_prompt_set_v1.csv (50 example prompts from today)

Next steps I propose:
1) You send the top 200 queries (or a representative sample) for a quick regression run (I can share a secure upload link).
2) We schedule a 30-minute follow-up to walk the detailed benchmark numbers and pick a canary configuration (suggest Wed/Thu this week).
3) If procurement needs rough pricing for budgeting, I can share a 3-month projection for each model variant.

Would next Wednesday 06/17 10:00am PT work for a follow-up?

Thanks —
Marissa Cole

Hey team — quick engineering notes to answer Jordan's questions about p95 and multi-turn behavior: 

- Measured p95 (public cloud Dedicated pool, 80GB A10G equiv):
  • Llama-3 8B (4-bit): p50 ~100ms, p95 ~350ms for single-turn generation (depends heavily on token length). Observed tail increases when context length >512 tokens.
  • Redwood-2 13B (FP16): p50 ~180ms, p95 ~420-550ms (better consistency on longer contexts due to runtime optimizations).
  • Mistral-Instruct 7B (8-bit): p50 ~95ms, p95 ~300ms. Good tail behavior for short-to-medium contexts.

- Multi-turn summarization: 13B shows noticeably fewer truncation/hallucination cases on the 4-8 turn logs we sampled. Llama-3 8B did well on intent and short answers but required prompt-tuning and a couple example-shot patterns to match 13B quality on summaries. We estimate a 5-12% drop in ROUGE-style metrics on longer summarization without prompt tuning; after prompt tuning that gap reduces to 1-4% in our evals.

- Canary recommendation: Start with Llama-3 8B quantized at 10% traffic for 72 hours, monitor quality regressions on the supplied prompt set + production sample. If p95 exceeds SLA for customer-facing flows, fallback to Redwood-2 13B for those routes automatically.

If you want, I can export a small dashboard with the p50/p95 histograms for each model and a per-route cost projection.

—Aditya
